hints: Since $4+x^2$ is an irreducible quadratic, start with $\frac{A}{1+x}+\frac{Bx+C}{4+x^2}$.
Clear the denominators to obtain a polynomial identity in $x$.
Use $x=-1$ to find $A$, then compare the $x^2$, $x$, and constant coefficients to determine $B$ and $C$.
Recombine the fractions to check the original numerator $-7x^2+2x-6$.
walkthrough:
Set up the partial fraction decomposition for a linear denominator and an irreducible quadratic denominator:
$$\dfrac{-7x^2 + 2x - 6}{(1 + x)(4 + x^2)} = \dfrac{A}{1 + x} + \dfrac{Bx + C}{4 + x^2}$$

Clear fractions by multiplying both sides by $(1 + x)(4 + x^2)$:
$$-7x^2 + 2x - 6 = A(4 + x^2) + (Bx + C)(1 + x)$$

Equate the coefficients of $x^2$ on both sides to solve for $B$:
$$-7 = A + B$$
$$-7 = -3 + B \implies B = -7 + 3 = -4$$

State the complete partial fraction decomposition:
$$f(x) = -\dfrac{3}{1 + x} + \dfrac{-4x + 6}{4 + x^2} = -\dfrac{3}{1 + x} - \dfrac{4x}{4 + x^2} + \dfrac{6}{4 + x^2}$$

hints: Integrate the partial fractions from part (a) term by term, separating the numerator $-4x+6$ over $x^2+4$.
Match the $-4x$ term to the derivative of $x^2+4$ for a logarithm, and use $\int\frac{dx}{x^2+a^2}=\frac1a\tan^{-1}(x/a)$ for the constant numerator.
Evaluate the complete antiderivative at $2$ and $0$, using $\tan^{-1}(1)=\pi/4$.
Combine the logarithms into the requested exact form rather than using decimals.
walkthrough:
Split the definite integral into three standard parts using the result of part (a):
$$\int_0^2 f(x)\,\mathrm{d}x = \int_0^2 \left( -\dfrac{3}{1 + x} - \dfrac{4x}{4 + x^2} + \dfrac{6}{4 + x^2} \right)\,\mathrm{d}x$$

Integrate each of the three terms separately:
$$\int -\dfrac{3}{1 + x}\,\mathrm{d}x = -3\ln|1 + x|$$
$$\int -\dfrac{4x}{4 + x^2}\,\mathrm{d}x = -2\int \dfrac{2x}{4 + x^2}\,\mathrm{d}x = -2\ln(4 + x^2)$$
$$\int \dfrac{6}{4 + x^2}\,\mathrm{d}x = 6\left(\dfrac{1}{2}\tan^{-1}\left(\dfrac{x}{2}\right)\right) = 3\tan^{-1}\left(\dfrac{x}{2}\right)$$

Combine the terms to form the complete antiderivative:
$$\left[ -3\ln(1 + x) - 2\ln(4 + x^2) + 3\tan^{-1}\left(\dfrac{x}{2}\right) \right]_0^2$$

Evaluate the antiderivative at the upper limit $x = 2$:
$$-3\ln(1 + 2) - 2\ln(4 + 2^2) + 3\tan^{-1}\left(\dfrac{2}{2}\right)$$
$$= -3\ln 3 - 2\ln(4 + 4) + 3\tan^{-1}(1)$$
$$= -3\ln 3 - 2\ln 8 + 3\left(\dfrac{\pi}{4}\right)$$
$$= -3\ln 3 - 2\ln(2^3) + \dfrac{3\pi}{4} = \dfrac{3\pi}{4} - 3\ln 3 - 6\ln 2$$

Evaluate the antiderivative at the lower limit $x = 0$:
$$-3\ln(1 + 0) - 2\ln(4 + 0^2) + 3\tan^{-1}\left(\dfrac{0}{2}\right)$$
$$= -3\ln 1 - 2\ln 4 + 3\tan^{-1}(0)$$
$$= -3(0) - 2\ln(2^2) + 0 = -4\ln 2$$

Subtract the lower limit value from the upper limit value:
$$\left(\dfrac{3\pi}{4} - 3\ln 3 - 6\ln 2\right) - (-4\ln 2)$$
$$= \dfrac{3\pi}{4} - 3\ln 3 - 6\ln 2 + 4\ln 2$$
$$= \dfrac{3\pi}{4} - 3\ln 3 - 2\ln 2$$

Combine the logarithmic terms using logarithmic laws:
$$-3\ln 3 - 2\ln 2 = -[\ln(3^3) + \ln(2^2)] = -[\ln 27 + \ln 4] = -\ln(27 \times 4) = -\ln 108$$

State the exact result in the form $a\pi - \ln b$:
$$\int_0^2 f(x)\,\mathrm{d}x = \dfrac{3\pi}{4} - \ln 108$$
